explanations.url_present: Has a link. Scams almost always try to get you to tap one.
explanations.url_shortener: Uses a link shortener, which hides where the link really goes.
explanations.suspicious_tld: The link ends in a web address type (like .top or .xyz) that's cheap and common in scams.
explanations.brand_lookalike: The link uses a company's name but isn't that company's real website.
explanations.ip_url: The link is a raw number address instead of a real website name.
explanations.urgency: Pressures you to act fast. Real companies rarely give you minutes or hours.
explanations.prize: Promises a prize or reward you didn't sign up for.
explanations.payment_ask: Mentions paying with gift cards, crypto, or money apps, which scammers prefer because it can't be reversed.
explanations.credential_ask: Asks you to verify or enter account details, codes, or passwords.
explanations.delivery_issue: Claims there's a problem with a package. One of the most common scam texts.
explanations.account_problem: Says your account is locked, suspended, or had unusual activity.
explanations.unpaid_bill: Claims you owe a toll, fine, or bill.
explanations.reply_to_claim: Asks you to text a short code or call a premium number, which can charge you.
explanations.shouting: Lots of ALL CAPS, a common trick to grab attention.
explanations.has_money: Mentions a specific amount of money.
explanations.has_phone: Includes a phone number to call.
